text:
maya: Heads-up — hosted API p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~760ms around 14:12 UTC, p99 ~1.8s. Alert from control-plane. Anyone seeing matching traces?

sre-bot: Alert: hosted.api.p95 > 700ms for 11m — route: /v1/generate — sample traces attached to incident 3529007

alex: grabbing traces now. linking flamegraphs and kernel selector logs.

chris: I see sustained queue depth rising on the front-end LB at the same time. Series: queue_len_hosted_api (avg windows): 6 -> 22 -> 40. Rate stayed flat. :thinking:

jen: interesting — batching metrics show an increase in batch latency. avg batch assembly time spiked from 12ms -> 110ms at ~14:11. Could be batching heuristic misfiring.

liam: profiler snapshot (short):
```
CPU: host-runtime-core
Top stacks:
  runtime::dispatch_kernel  34.7%
  batching::assemble_batch   21.1%
  kvcache::lookup           12.3%
  kernel_selector::score     8.9%
  aux_kernel::fallback      3.4%
```
Notable: kernel_selector is taking locks while KV lookup is in progress -> contention.

maya: ops timeline: we rolled a kernel selector tweak at 13:45 (kselector v2). It changed affinity thresholds and enabled prefetch probing on warmup. Could be correlated.

alex: reproducer command for a small test load: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s -s api_gen.lua --latency http://hosted-api.internal/v1/generate` — try with the rollout and previous kselector.

chris: i ran a narrow A/B on a single pool — kselector v2 shows higher batch-assembly latency and more KV cache evictions. When I disable prefetch probing, p95 drops ~40%.

jen: log snippet from runtime pool 5 around spike:
```
[14:11:53] batch_assemble: waiting_for_kv(tenant=acct-432) wait_ms=98
[14:11:53] kselector: affinity_check took=65ms decision=aux_kernel
[14:11:54] kvcache: evict keyset tenant=acct-432 freed=12
[14:11:54] batch_dispatch: dispatched=1 batch_size=4 latency_ms=110
```
Seems like prefetch->evict loop: prefetch probes cause extra KV pressure on hot tenant, eviction leads to misses, then bigger assembly waits.

liam: also saw noisy-tenant pattern: tenant acct-432 had a burst of short requests that force small batches -> batch assembler spins and kernel selector repeatedly evals. Kernel selector does a relatively expensive scoring pass (costly locks) per candidate on small batches -> linear blow-up.

maya: Rate-limiter config for that tenant was loosened earlier this week (temp increase burst tokens). That could let microbursts through that used to be smoothed.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback kselector v2 to v1, 2) disable prefetch probing globally, 3) tighten burst tokens for suspect tenant, 4) enable aux-kernel fallback earlier to avoid selector scoring in hot path. Which do we want to try first?

chris: I can flip prefetch -> off for a single host pool (low risk) and watch p95. If it drops, we can consider staged rollback.

jen: Also want to throttle batch assembly concurrency: limit concurrent assemble workers to reduce lock contention. That should reduce tail even if throughput suffers slightly.

maya: quick A/B results from chris: prefetch off on pool-5 -> p95 dropped from 760ms -> 260ms within 90s. Queue depth normalized.

liam: added flame snapshot after prefetch off:
```
  runtime::dispatch_kernel  29.1%
  batching::assemble_batch   11.2%
  kvcache::lookup            9.8%
  kernel_selector::score     3.1%
```
Selector cost massively reduced.

ops-bot: Change executed: prefetch probing toggled OFF on pool-5 by @chris at 14:25 UTC.

maya: Good catch. Next steps:
- short-term: keep prefetch probing off on all hosted pools until we have a perf-safe redesign (ACTION: chris to run canary across 3 pools, ETA 1h)
- medium: revert kselector v2 or rework scoring to avoid locks during KV lookups (ACTION: alex + liam to propose patch, ETA 2 days)
- cluster ops: tighten burst tokens for identified noisy tenants and add protective per-tenant batching windows (ACTION: jen to draft config change, ETA 4h)
- instrumentation: add metric for "kselector_score_latency" and "batch_assemble_wait_for_kv_ms" (ACTION: maya to open observability ticket, ETA 1d)

alex: I'll start a bisect job to compare v1 vs v2 on identical traffic.

chris: I'll roll prefetch off to two additional pools now, monitoring dashboards. Posting live link: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/api/p95/dash?panel=queue_len

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread as the incident anchor. tagging @oncall for postmortem. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident 3529007 assigned -> eng-runtime. Postmortem template created at /incidents/3529007.

maya: closing with note: root cause likely interplay of kselector v2 prefetch probing + loosened tenant burst limits -> KV cache churn -> batch-assembly contention -> queue depth growth -> p95/p99 spike. We'll track fixes and reopen if spike recurs.
